This confirms robust AR engagement by enzalutamide and androgen suppression by leuprolide. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The downstream biology (androgen-driven tumor proliferation suppression) was clearly modulated. PSA suppression rates and time-to-PSA-progression data confirm that the androgen signaling pathway was effectively suppressed in both treatment arms. The combination arm showed superior pathway suppression compared to monotherapy. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary endpoint (MFS) was met with HR 0.424 (95% CI 0.296-0.607), p<0.0001 for enzalutamide+leuprolide vs placebo+leuprolide. Enzalutamide monotherapy also met MFS with HR 0.631, p=0.0049. Multiple secondary endpoints (time to PSA progression, time to castration resistance, time to symptomatic progression, time to first SSE) all showed significant benefit. The biology clearly translated to clinical benefit. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses were reported. Both treatment arms succeeded, with the combination showing stronger effects than monotherapy, consistent with the mechanistic hypothesis that leuprolide amplifies enzalutamide's efficacy by reducing circulating androgens. 5. CONFOUNDERS: No major confounders identified. The trial was large (N=1068), well-powered, and had a long follow-up (~425 weeks). Safety signals (cardiovascular events, seizures) are consistent with known enzalutamide and ADT class effects but did not prevent adequate dosing or require trial termination. The dose-modification protocol (treatment suspension at Week 37 for undetectable PSA) reflects an adaptive design feature, not a safety-driven dose reduction. No dose-limiting toxicity prevented adequate target engagement.
